title: ApiSpecItems
description: Shape of content.items for L1-design-api-spec. The artifact (openapi.yaml) is the authoritative, machine-readable contract; items restates the same facts in queryable structured form so downstream agents (L1-design-hld, L1-design-lld, L1-testing-script-generator, both construction code generators) can read traceability without parsing YAML. Three arrays, each enforcing one half of a bidirectional no-orphans rule: endpoints[] proves no endpoint exists without an FR behind it (fr_trace is minItems 1), fr_coverage[] proves no FR was silently dropped from the surface (one entry per FR, same ids and same order as requirements.md), and open_questions[] proves every TBD NFR boundary condition survived as a documented gap rather than being resolved into a plausible number. A TBD that appears as a concrete value anywhere in the contract is a schema-level failure of this agent's core discipline, not a style preference — mirroring the zero-tolerance rule L1-requirements-nfr-classifier's own schema sets for fabricated boundary values.

endpoints.description: One entry per operation (method + path pair) in openapi.yaml. Every entry must trace to at least one FR — an endpoint with no FR behind it is an invented endpoint.

fr_coverage.description: One entry per functional requirement in requirements.md, same FR ids and same order — never grouped, never reordered, never omitted. An FR that genuinely produces no endpoint (a UI-only or reporting-only requirement) is recorded with coverage 'non_api' and a rationale, never dropped.

open_questions.description: Every TBD carried into the contract as an x-open-question extension, plus any HLD/OpenAPI reconciliation disagreement. May be empty only if nfr-spec.md contained no TBD boundary condition at all — which, given the classifier marks genuinely-ungrounded conditions TBD by design, is rare and should be visible in reasoning.

hld_reconciliation.description: Present ONLY when hld_output was supplied. One entry per HLD API-NN and per openapi.yaml path, showing which side each appears on. Absent entirely when the agent ran without an HLD, which is the normal case today — no HLD producer exists in the greenfield pipeline.

NfrTrace.description: One nfr-spec.md boundary condition and the specific place in the contract it shaped. A boundary condition that changed nothing in the contract does not belong here; a contract detail with no boundary condition or KB rule behind it does not belong in the contract.

category.description: The nfr-spec.md category this condition was classified under — carried through unchanged, never re-classified here

boundary_condition.description: The boundary condition verbatim from nfr-spec.md, including the literal 'TBD — needs stakeholder input' phrasing when it is still open. Never reworded, never resolved into a number.

applied_as.description: Where in the contract this condition landed. 'open_question' is the ONLY valid value when boundary_condition is TBD — a TBD may never become a security_scheme value, a rate_limit_note number, or any other concrete contract detail.

source.description: 'nfr-spec.md § FR-NNN' when the condition came from the classifier's output for that FR; 'kb-L1-enterprise-security § ES<n>' or 'kb-L1-enterprise-architecture § EA<n>' when an enterprise rule shaped the contract directly (e.g. ES1's external-IdP rule, EA2's Gateway-first rule) rather than arriving through a per-FR condition.

operation_id.description: camelCase, matching the operationId in openapi.yaml exactly — the join key downstream agents use

method.description: Lowercase, matching OpenAPI's own path-item key casing

path.description: Versioned, plural, kebab-case resource path per the REST conventions embedded in instructions.md — e.g. /v1/producers/{producerId}/traceability-records

summary.description: One line, matching the operation's summary in openapi.yaml

fr_trace.description: Every FR-NNN that motivated this endpoint. minItems 1 is the schema-level enforcement of 'no endpoint without an FR behind it' — an endpoint the agent thinks is obviously needed but cannot trace is an invented endpoint and must not be emitted.

nfr_trace.description: Boundary conditions that shaped this endpoint's auth, rate limit, error shape, retention, method restrictions or schema constraints. May be empty if the FR's classification carried no condition touching this endpoint — never padded with conditions that changed nothing.

auth.description: The securityScheme name applied to this operation in openapi.yaml, or the literal 'none (public)' for a genuinely unauthenticated operation. Per kb-L1-enterprise-security ES1 an external-facing scheme is never Azure AD, and any compliance-relevant write is tied to a non-shared authenticated identity — a 'none (public)' on such an operation is a defect, not a choice.

reasoning.description: Why this resource/method shape follows from the cited FR's verbatim statement, and why each NFR condition landed where it did — not a restatement of the FR itself

id.description: The requirements.md FR id — never a new id, this agent derives a contract, it does not create requirements

coverage.description: 'covered' when >=1 endpoint implements this FR; 'non_api' when the FR genuinely has no API surface (a UI-only interaction, or a constraint on the whole surface rather than an operation on it). There is deliberately no 'uncovered' value — an FR with no endpoint and no rationale for why is a dropped requirement, which this agent must not be able to express.

operation_ids.description: operation_ids from endpoints[] implementing this FR. Non-empty if and only if coverage is 'covered'.

rationale.description: For 'covered', why these operations fully implement the FR. For 'non_api', why the FR has no API surface at all — a specific argument from the FR's own statement, never a generic 'not applicable'.

question.description: The decision a stakeholder has to make, phrased so it can be answered — not a restatement of 'this is TBD'

origin.description: 'nfr_tbd' — a TBD boundary condition carried through from nfr-spec.md. 'hld_reconciliation' — an API-NN/path disagreement between the HLD and openapi.yaml, raised rather than silently resolved in either direction (only possible when hld_output was supplied). 'requirements_gap' — the FR statement itself leaves a contract detail undefined (e.g. the bounds of a score it references).

source_fr.description: The FR whose derivation surfaced this question. '—' is valid ONLY for an origin of 'hld_reconciliation' where the HLD element in question has no FR behind it at all — which is itself the finding: an HLD API-NN that traces to no requirement is exactly the disagreement that must be raised rather than resolved by silently emitting the endpoint. For 'nfr_tbd' and 'requirements_gap' a real FR id is always available, since both originate in the FR walk.

spec_location.description: Where the x-open-question extension sits in openapi.yaml — a JSON-pointer-ish path such as '/paths/~1v1~1producers/get/x-open-question' or '/components/schemas/CompletenessScore/x-open-question'. Every open question MUST be visible in the artifact itself, not only in items; a question recorded here but absent from the YAML is invisible to the five downstream consumers that read the YAML rather than these items. A question about something deliberately NOT in the contract (an HLD API-NN with no FR behind it) still needs somewhere to live — use '/info/x-open-question', the document-level list.

hld_api_id.description: The HLD's API-NN id, or '—' for a path that exists only in openapi.yaml

path.description: The openapi.yaml path, or the HLD's stated path for an API-NN with no openapi.yaml counterpart

open_question_id.description: Required whenever present_in_hld and present_in_openapi disagree — the disagreement becomes an open question, never a silent resolution in either direction
